enums.name: Format
enums.help: An image file format. `Avif` is the AVIF format, and `Jxl` is the JPEG XL format. `Image::withFormat` sets the format of the file that `encode` returns. `encode` runs every step you added to the image and returns the finished file. `Image::open` reads all eight formats. `encode` writes only `Jpeg`, `Png`, `Webp`, `Gif` and `Avif`.

enums.name: Gravity
enums.help: A position in an image, written as a direction from the center. Image programs call this position the gravity. `North` is the top, `East` is the right, `South` is the bottom and `West` is the left. `resized`, `withOverlay` and `withText` use it to place the image or the text. When `resized` cuts off part of the image, it keeps the part at this position. The default is `Center`.

enums.name: Fit
enums.help: How `resized` fits an image into a box of the width and height you give. `Cover` fills the whole box and cuts off what does not fit. It is the default. `Contain` shows the whole image in the box, and the empty part is transparent. `Fill` stretches the image to the size of the box, so its shape changes. `Inside` keeps the whole image and its shape, and the result is no larger than the box. `Outside` keeps the whole image and its shape, and the result is no smaller than the box.

enums.name: Filter
enums.help: The filter `resized` uses to calculate the new pixels. A faster filter gives a softer result, and a slower filter keeps more detail. `Nearest` is the fastest. It copies the closest pixel and keeps hard edges, so it suits pixel art. `Bilinear` is fast, and the result is a little soft. `CatmullRom` and `Mitchell` are slower and sharper than `Bilinear`. `Lanczos3` is the slowest and keeps the most detail. It is the default.

enums.name: Axis
enums.help: The direction in which `flipped` mirrors an image. `Horizontal` swaps left and right, and `Vertical` swaps top and bottom.

enums.name: Blend
enums.help: How `withOverlay` mixes the colours of the image on top with the colours of the image below it. `Normal` puts the top image over the lower one. It is the default. `Multiply` makes the result darker. White on top changes nothing. `Screen` makes the result lighter. Black on top changes nothing. `Overlay` makes dark parts darker and light parts lighter, so the contrast is higher. `Darken` keeps the darker of the two values for each of red, green and blue. `Lighten` keeps the lighter of the two values for each of red, green and blue.

enums.name: Align
enums.help: How `withText` and `Image::measureText` line up the lines of a text. The default is `Left`.

enums.name: Output
enums.help: What `Codec::run` returns: the encoded file, the RGBA8 pixels, or the size alone.

enums.name: HashKind
enums.help: The kind of hash `Image::hash` returns. An image hash is a short value that describes what an image looks like. Two similar images have almost the same hash. A `Perceptual` hash is 8 bytes and is based on the large shapes of the image. A `Difference` hash is 16 bytes and is based on where the image gets brighter or darker. An `Average` hash is 32 bytes and is based on which parts are brighter than the image as a whole.

enums.name: PlaceholderKind
enums.help: The kind of placeholder `Image::placeholder` returns. A placeholder is a short text that a web page draws as a blurred preview while the real image loads. `BlurHash` and `ThumbHash` are two formats for this text. The browser decodes each format with a small script made for it. A `BlurHash` is 28 characters and has no transparency. A `ThumbHash` is base64 text and also keeps transparency.

enums.name: Level
enums.help: How much of a QR code can be damaged and still be read. A QR code stores extra data to repair the parts that a scanner cannot read. This is called error correction. `Low` repairs about 7 percent of the code, and `Medium` about 15 percent. `Quartile` repairs about 25 percent, which is a quarter of the code. `High` repairs about 30 percent. The default is `Medium`. A higher level makes a bigger code for the same data.

enums.name: Symbology
enums.help: The barcode format that `Barcode::render` and `Barcode::svg` draw. A barcode format is also called a symbology. `Ean13` and `UpcA` are the barcodes on products in shops. `UpcA` is used in North America. `Ean8` is the short form for small products. `Itf14` is the barcode on a shipping box. `Code128` and `Code39` contain text, such as a tracking number. `Gs1128` contains standard fields, such as a product number and a batch number. `DataMatrix` is a square code. The others are lines of bars.
